original_question: Given a Diophantine equation, determine whether it has at least one integer solution.
target_in_paper: Section 6, Problem 6 ("Existence of integer solutions"), i.e. the paper’s Hilbert 10th problem formulation. ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2404.08518v5))
correct_elements: Your draft captures the paper’s core existential decision problem almost verbatim: it asks whether a Diophantine equation has at least one integer solution. It also correctly focuses on existence, rather than on parametrizing all solutions, describing them explicitly, or deciding finiteness/infinitude. ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2404.08518v5))
missing_details: The paper’s term here is a single polynomial Diophantine equation P(x1,...,xd)=0 with integer coefficients, not an arbitrary non-polynomial equation or a system of equations. ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2404.08518v5))

It is implicit from Section 1 that the equation has at least one variable: the paper assumes at least one monomial is non-constant. ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2404.08518v5))
The ambient solution domain should be stated explicitly as integer tuples in Z^d. ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2404.08518v5))

Problem 6 is unrestricted with respect to degree, homogeneity, symmetry, cyclicity, number of monomials, and number of variables; those are separate categories introduced elsewhere in the paper, not assumptions of this problem. ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2404.08518v5))

For a stand-alone formulation, it is helpful to state the quantifier explicitly: decide whether there exists at least one tuple (x1,...,xd) in Z^d satisfying P(x1,...,xd)=0. ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2404.08518v5))

There is no extra asymptotic clause, operator condition, nilpotency condition, or positivity restriction in Problem 6; in fact, the positive-integer variant is separated out later as Problem 7. ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2404.08518v5))
refined_question: Given a single polynomial Diophantine equation P(x1,...,xd)=0, where P belongs to Z[x1,...,xd] and has at least one nonconstant monomial (so d>=1), decide whether there exists an integer tuple (x1,...,xd) in Z^d such that P(x1,...,xd)=0. No restriction on degree, homogeneity, symmetry, cyclicity, or number of monomials is assumed. ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2404.08518v5))
justification: The nearest official formulation is Problem 6 itself, because your draft matches its existential-solvability wording directly. It is closer than Problems 2, 4, and 5, which ask about arbitrarily large solutions, finiteness versus infinitude, or nontrivial solutions to homogeneous equations, and it is also distinct from Problem 7, which asks for positive-integer solutions. Section 1 explicitly frames non-emptiness of the integer solution set as one of the paper’s guiding questions, and Section 6 then states that question formally as Problem 6. The paper does not present a nearer formulation under labels such as Conjecture 1.1, Proposition 1.2, or Theorem 1.3; the relevant paper-faithful target is this numbered problem. ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2404.08518v5))
